headline: IM Cannabis names Ronen Zalayet CEO as Oren Shuster resigns
dek: IM Cannabis changed CEO on 19 November and pointed to technology businesses, days before a 1-for-3 share consolidation on 23 November.
key_points: IM Cannabis appointed Ronen Zalayet, a financial executive and Israeli CPA, as chief executive effective 19 November, succeeding Oren Shuster, who also left the board.
The company tied the change to its goal of building technology-driven businesses beyond its core medical cannabis operations; it gave no reason for Shuster's resignation.
Shakked Shuster becomes CEO of the Israeli subsidiary Focus Medical Herbs, and Ohad Melnik joins the board subject to approval by Israel's medical cannabis agency.
A 1-for-3 consolidation is expected to take effect on Nasdaq on 23 November, cutting shares outstanding from about 1.84 million to about 615,000.
body: IM Cannabis Corp., the Nasdaq-listed medical cannabis company with its main operations in Israel, has changed its chief executive. In a release filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on 20 November, the company said Ronen Zalayet became CEO on 19 November, succeeding Oren Shuster, who resigned as chief executive and as a director the same day.

The company framed the move as part of a strategy shift. Its release says the appointments fit a previously stated goal of evaluating and building technology-driven businesses beyond its core medical cannabis operations. It gives no reason for Shuster's departure. The change comes four days before a 1-for-3 share consolidation, the company's second in three months, that is meant to keep its stock above Nasdaq's US$1.00 minimum bid.

Zalayet is a finance executive rather than a cannabis operator. According to the release, he has more than 25 years in financial leadership at private and public companies. He has been chief financial officer of Nexera Technologies, the Nasdaq-listed company formerly called Jeffs' Brands, since October 2022. He was CEO and a director of Shemen Oil and Gas Resources on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange from July 2021 to December 2023, and CFO of Fort Technology, formerly Impact Acquisition Corp., from July 2025 to June 2026.

Earlier, he was CFO of Colugo Systems from 2019 to 2021 and ran the Israeli office of Access Capital Markets between 2016 and 2020. He holds economics, accounting and MBA degrees from Tel Aviv University and is an Israeli certified public accountant.
> When a cannabis company hands the top job to a capital-markets CFO, the next chapter is usually written in the financing, not the greenhouse.

Oren Shuster stays on the boards of the company's Israeli subsidiaries. Shakked Shuster takes over as CEO of Focus Medical Herbs, the Israeli subsidiary, also from 19 November. The release says Shakked Shuster joined in July 2020 as a product marketing lead and later headed product and marketing, before working as a consultant and then returning full-time to the Israeli operations in May 2026.

Ohad Melnik joins the board, filling the seat left by Einat Zakariya, who resigned in September. His appointment needs approval from the Israel Medical Cannabis Agency, and the board considers him independent under Nasdaq rules. Melnik was a director of Formula Systems from 2019 to 2024 and has worked in online payments and finance compliance at the iFOREX group.

The consolidation is the backdrop to all of this. As we reported on 19 November, IM Cannabis plans to swap every three existing shares for one new share. In its 18 November release, the company said the change is expected to take effect at the market open on 23 November, subject to Nasdaq confirmation, cutting the share count from 1,844,162 to about 614,721. The ticker stays IMCC; the CUSIP and ISIN numbers change.

The company already carried out a 30-for-1 consolidation on 27 August. Nasdaq's rules say a company that has done a reverse split in the past year does not get the usual 180-day grace period to regain compliance. If the closing bid stays below US$1.00 for 30 business days in a row, Nasdaq staff would issue a delisting determination, the company warned. By MetaFlora's arithmetic, the two consolidations together turn 90 old shares into one new share.

The leadership change and the stated push into technology suggest the board is looking for a business that capital markets will value more highly than an Israel-focused medical cannabis business. The release does not name any target, deal or product. A CEO with long experience as a public-company CFO, including at a former SPAC, fits a company whose immediate priorities are its listing and its funding.

For Israeli patients and partners, the day-to-day business at Focus Medical Herbs stays under Shakked Shuster, with Oren Shuster still on the subsidiaries' boards. For shareholders, the question is whether the consolidation holds the price above US$1.00 long enough to keep the Nasdaq listing.

On 23 November the 1-for-3 consolidation is due to take effect on Nasdaq. After that, watch the closing bid against the US$1.00 line over the following 30 business days, Israel's decision on Melnik's board seat, and any announcement that puts substance behind the technology strategy.
